I probably remember it wrong, but I once read one of those stories of game design ingenuity about the original Quake, about how when you fire the rocket launcher, the missile actually spawns right behind you, because it turns out to optimize both game performance and the felt rhythm of play.

DOOM (2016) pulls this kind of tricks all the time. The game will snap you a small distance in space to make you feel and look good, giving you that last inch to grab a ledge, or letting you activate a finishing move at the last possible second, right when you most need the health boost it dispenses. Jonathan Blow talks about "generosity" as a design value, when you take a player gesture or affordance that might typically be kept scarce to make it exciting (such as time rewinds in Prince of Persia) and make it available all the time. DOOM is not a comprehensively generous game: it understands the micro-narrative impact of running out of railgun rounds two-thirds through a fight and having to revise your tactics in response (or taking a different approach on the next reload). But it is generous about the core experience of dancing around and shredding up hellspawn: you always have a shot, and it always look sick as shit.

Doom is a fast-pace combat oriented FPS . The solo campaign on normal difficulty (“Hurt me Plenty”) was a very enjoyable experience. The level design is varied and interesting. The music suits the different moments well. The guns feel great. The combat is intense and fun.

The multiplayer is still active ("Team Play" playlist) on weekends as of writing this (edit : 19/06/2022). You may need to be patient to find a game. Lots of veterans are still playing so the learning curve will be a bit steep (prepare to get stomped a lot). The different game modes ("Team Play") are all fun to play. Unlocking all the guns, equipment and runes doesn’t take much time. You can then focus on learning the maps and improving your skills !

All 3 of the modern Doom games are perfect in their own ways. My only complaint in this game is that level 2 is the hardest level on nightmare mode by far and then the game gets much easier. There's just one room of soldiers and imps that seems unfair. Other than that it was an amazing experience.

Everything feels good. The perk system works, but the only aspect of this game that falls a little bit behind is weapon upgrade system. Some of these upgrades are necessary for the proper function of the weapon, but there are also unnecessary upgrades. For example, why does combat shotgun have charged burst, when it becomes completely useless when you get double barell shotgun? Why would you pick that weapon upgrade in the first place, when you can pick explosive shot right away? I´m not going to name the useless weapon ugrades on all weapons, but every weapon has one.

Multiplayer is awesome, however, it lives in the shadow of the singleplayer campaign. It still has it´s players, so you can hop in and play few matches right away. The player upgrade system is allright, but the suit customization menu could have been simplified at least a little bit.

Overall, this is one of the greatest games ever made, and succeeds in what the first two DOOM games established- fun gameplay, pure action and gore.

A true successor to the classics in almost every way. The campaign is pure violence and speed, while leaving the plot deceptively simple. You hate demons. Kill all the demons. Stop the invasion. Get guns, kill demons, get bigger guns, kill bigger demons, GO TO HELL, kill the biggest demon with the BIGGEST FUCKING GUN.

But there's way more going on here if you go out of your way to find it....

The multiplayer is also SERIOUSLY underrated. Each player gets a two-weapon loadout plus an Equipment item. It's all about "weapon swapping", and mechanically speaking works a lot like a Mortal Kombat move - a series of properly timed button presses can absolutely destroy a player in a split second, possibly even groups of them if you know what to do. But plenty of players know how to do the same to you. It had its flaws at launch and the less-than-familiar Arena Shooter newbs that reviewed it didn't play more than two games to make a proper judgement, but it's a blast once you get the hang of it.

I paid full price for the base game and all its DLC about 2 weeks after launch (that's $100, btw) and I absolutely think it was worth it. Now that it's cheaper, it's an even better bang for your buck.

DOOM is a must play for any FPS fan. Truly a game that defines PC gaming as a whole. The campaign is classic DOOM with the right amount of modern touches. Definitely a revival of what FPS should be. If you enjoy high paced action FPS games with an core focus on gameplay rather than a 50 hour walking simulator with too many cutscenes, DOOM is an absolute must buy. No reloading, Movement is key, No shortage of demons to rip and tear. There are some repetitive features such as; the demon variations not changing much late in the game and some redundant weapon mods. Overall. DOOM (2016) shows the industry what FPS is truly meant to be.

A no nonsense shooter from a bygone era. This game is so good. The missions are all expertly crafted, the dialogue is minimal while still making you feel like a total badass and the gunplay is amazing and the graphics look better than most games releasing today. In the era of everything being a live service game or having a loot system tacked on to increase engagement it is incredibly refreshing to play a game that focuses more on the level and enemy interactions than "big number goes up" especially considering I am coming from years of playing Destiny 2 and looking for something worthwhile to fill that void. If you're feeling burned out on modern shooters but don't want to go back and play something from the early 2000s this game manages to be the best of both worlds. Honestly for $20 I'd say more than worth it, and if you can get it on sale even better.

While killing demons with some badass music is extremely satisfying, I started to get bored after just 8 hours. And i found a couple answers as to why this happened to me.

First of all, Glory killing is badass but its the lack of variations that really got me. While being able to brutally kill demons It is mostly the same couple of animations, I just couldnt feel the Hype anymore because it just felt too repetitive

What I also found boring was the lack of movement. The only thing thats available is just jumping, literally. No advanced mechanics like dashing, wall-running or anything like that. It just felt too slow when all i had was running for a fast paced combat game.

Except these two flaws it is a pretty cool game that i enjoyed overall.
